post.caption: Anglo-Saxon royal garnets traveled thousands of miles. They come from a ship burial at Sutton Hoo in Suffolk, which dates to around 625 and was found in 1939. Its gold shoulder clasps hold garnets and glass. Each garnet is a thin polished plate set in a gold cell, a technique called cloisonné. Beneath each garnet is wafer thin gold foil stamped with a pattern, and the foil bounces light back so the stone glows. In 2023 early scans traced some garnets to India and Sri Lanka. Other garnets were traced to Czechia. The British Museum says the trip covered thousands of miles.
